title: Datasets and dataloaders, and the GPU sitting idle waiting for data

videos.script: Lesson 9 cut its batches by hand, out of two tensors already in memory. {{slicing}} Real data is rarely that tidy. It is a folder of files, each one decoded and changed before use. {{folder}} PyTorch splits that job in two. A dataset says how many items there are, and hands back item number i. {{dataset}} A data loader picks the order, cuts it into batches and stacks the items together. {{loader}} Then the digits get a transform that does real work. Each one is enlarged, bent and given noise. {{warp}} Reading one image becomes hundreds of times slower than reading it plain. {{cost}} Worker processes can build the next batches while the model trains on this one. {{workers}} A clock on every batch splits the epoch into two parts: waiting, and computing. {{clock}} On a graphics card, the computing shrinks. The waiting does not. {{card}} That is the expensive card sitting idle, waiting for the processor to feed it. {{idle}} Last, the model and the batches move to the device, in a pattern that runs on either machine. {{end}}
